slides.headline: A HACKER WHO STOLE 4,000 BITCOIN LEFT ONE MESSAGE THROUGH THE BLOCKCHAIN: FIX THE BUG AND I'LL RETURN ALL $320 MILLION
slides.image_prompt: SUBJECT: A giant gold Bitcoin coin, 18 inches across on a real marble surface, mid-explosion as it cracks cleanly apart, smaller gold coins erupting outward in a frozen violent cascade, peak of the burst. BACKDROP PROPS: a blazing amber shockwave of cascading gold coins filling the upper frame; a single signal-blue glowing envelope the size of a hardback book floating calmly back toward the fractured coin — stillness against the chaos. PALETTE: blazing gold and signal orange. LABELS: "$320M" on a bold amber receipt-paper chip at the base of the cracked coin. Documentary news photo, 35mm, harsh on-camera flash, slight film grain. Real marble table surface, real physical coins — no digital renders, no sci-fi elements, bright saturated lighting throughout.

slides.headline: LIQUID NETWORK USERS WOKE UP THINKING THEIR BITCOIN WAS UNTOUCHABLE
slides.body:
The Liquid Network is a Bitcoin sidechain built for fast, private transfers.

Users trusted it. Their Bitcoin sat there like cash in a vault nobody thought to question. Until it wasn't

slides.headline: ONE ATTACK HIT EVERY NODE ON THE NETWORK
slides.body:
Every wallet on the Liquid sidechain exposed
Attacker found a crack nobody had patched
You wouldn't have had time to react
Then they got a message back.
Through the blockchain itself. And everyone could read it

slides.headline: THE MESSAGE IS PERMANENTLY WRITTEN INTO THE BLOCKCHAIN ITSELF
slides.body:
The hacker embedded a note into a Bitcoin transaction: fix the bug, patch every node, then the money comes back.

You can read it right now, the message is still live.

slides.headline: UNTIL THE BUG IS PATCHED, EVERY USER IS EXPOSED
slides.body:
Businesses that hold crypto on platforms like this have zero warning when the floor drops.

If yours does, ask one question: when was it last audited

slides.headline: SAVE THIS: A HACKER STOLE $320M AND TEXTED THE DEVS BACK
slides.body: Liquid Network hacked for $320 million Attacker drained 4,000 Bitcoin in one move Hacker messaged developers through the blockchain Message is public, permanent, on-chain Send to the friend with crypto in one place

caption:
Swipe to see how a hacker stole $320 million in Bitcoin then wrote a message to the developers inside the blockchain itself 🔐

The Liquid Network, a Bitcoin sidechain, was hit by a hack that drained 4,000 Bitcoin worth $320 million, the attacker used on-chain Bitcoin transactions to message the network's developers directly, the message demanded the vulnerability be patched before any funds are returned, the note is permanently embedded in the blockchain and visible to anyone, every user on the network remains exposed until the fix is deployed.

Blockchain transparency cuts both ways. The same public ledger a hacker exploits becomes the only place they can negotiate. Crypto security is only as strong as the last audit.
Running a business with digital assets? DM us 'AI' and we'll show you what this means for yours.

Sources: Watcher.Guru on X

#Bitcoin #CryptoHack #Blockchain #CryptoSecurity #Web3
